def lex_min_vertex_cover(n1, n2, edges):
    """
    Return the lexicographically smallest minimum vertex cover of a bipartite graph.

    The graph has left vertices labeled 1..n1 and right vertices labeled
    n1+1..n1+n2. `edges` is a list of pairs (u, v) with 1 <= u <= n1 and
    n1+1 <= v <= n1+n2; duplicate pairs may appear and are equivalent to a
    single edge. A vertex cover is a set of vertices containing at least one
    endpoint of every edge. Among all vertex covers of minimum possible size,
    return the one whose sorted list of labels is lexicographically smallest
    (covers are compared as sorted lists of ints, element by element; all
    minimum covers have equal length, so this order is total and the answer
    is unique -- there are no further ties to break). Return that cover as a
    sorted list of ints. If there are no edges, the answer is [].

    Bounds: 1 <= n1 <= 25, 1 <= n2 <= 25, 0 <= len(edges) <= 250.

    >>> lex_min_vertex_cover(2, 2, [(1, 3), (1, 4), (2, 4)])
    [1, 2]
    >>> lex_min_vertex_cover(2, 1, [(1, 3), (2, 3)])
    [3]
    >>> lex_min_vertex_cover(3, 2, [(1, 4), (2, 4), (2, 5), (3, 5)])
    [4, 5]
    """
